verdict.root_cause: The cart service stopped accepting connections at ~08:31 and its endpoint was withdrawn from service discovery. Checkout's traces show all 10 sampled PlaceOrder flows aborting on the first dependency call, GetCart, with client-side gRPC UNAVAILABLE from a resolver returning zero addresses — the request never reached a cart instance [tr_16de3a6a8892]. frontend's logs show the same transport failure against one fixed peer 172.18.0.19:7070, ECONNREFUSED around 08:29 degrading to EHOSTUNREACH by 08:33 — a host with nothing listening, then an address no longer routable [tr_ebb4459c8a52]. Error ratios at frontend and checkout were flat zero across the 32-minute baseline then stepped up at 08:31/08:32 [tr_e1386aed2206][tr_8ec587ee7e45]. No cart-side telemetry was collected, so the location of the fault is established but the mechanism that killed the cart process is not.
verdict.reasoning: The deepest erroring span in every trace is checkout's outbound GetCart; frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator carry ERROR only as inherited status with trivial self time, so the alerting services are reporters, not culprits [tr_16de3a6a8892]. Checkout is not the origin either: its self time is minimal, the error attaches to the client span, its change log is empty [tr_948b37be18cb], and it still serves ~33% of spans [tr_8ec587ee7e45]. frontend's socket-level ECONNREFUSED/EHOSTUNREACH against a single peer rules out latency, DNS, TLS and application-level errors [tr_ebb4459c8a52], converging with the trace evidence on cart being absent rather than slow or broken in its handler. The step onset rules out gradual saturation at the caller [tr_e1386aed2206]. Because no cart logs, metrics or change history were ever queried, a crash-looping bad artifact, an OOM kill, and an operator stop are all still consistent with this caller-side picture, so I name the service but not the mechanism.
open_questions: No cart-side evidence exists at all — cart logs, memory/restart metrics and change history were never queried; these would distinguish a crash-looping deploy, an OOM kill, and a deliberate stop.
Is 172.18.0.19:7070 actually cart? The frontend log names only an address, and no endpoint/DNS mapping was retrieved [tr_ebb4459c8a52].

Checkout's log stream returned zero lines for the whole window, which may indicate a broken log pipeline or label mismatch independent of this incident [tr_8c913248cd48]; change queries also covered only post-onset time, so a pre-08:31 change to cart or checkout would not appear [tr_85c449e104e6].

alternatives.root_cause: A bad cart deploy or image left the container unable to start, so it crash-loops and its endpoints are withdrawn.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible and fits the ECONNREFUSED→EHOSTUNREACH progression, but no change history for cart was ever queried, so there is no evidence of any artifact change.

alternatives.root_cause: The cart process was OOM-killed or hit a resource limit and died, taking its listener with it.
alternatives.why_not: The caller-side onset is a sharp step rather than a ramp [tr_8ec587ee7e45], which fits a sudden kill but no cart memory/CPU metrics were collected to confirm exhaustion.

alternatives.root_cause: Cart is running but severed from the network, so callers cannot reach it.
alternatives.why_not: ECONNREFUSED at onset means the host was reachable and actively rejecting the port — a partition would not refuse — so a dead listener fits better than a severed network.

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating cart should restore a listener on its gRPC port and its discovery endpoint. Within ~5 minutes: checkout's error ratio (same query as tr_8ec587ee7e45) falls from its post-08:32 level back toward the flat-zero baseline; frontend stops logging '14 UNAVAILABLE ... ECONNREFUSED/EHOSTUNREACH 172.18.0.19:7070'; new checkout traces show GetCart completing OK instead of failing sub-millisecond with a zero-address resolver error.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if after 5 minutes frontend still logs transport errors to 172.18.0.19:7070, checkout traces still abort at GetCart, or checkout's error ratio has not fallen. A container that exits again means a crash-looping image or OOM kill (needs rollback_image plus cart-side logs/metrics never collected); cart up but callers still seeing EHOSTUNREACH means a detached network, fixable only by reconnect_service, which this executor cannot do. Note the peer address was never mapped to cart via DNS/endpoint data, and checkout's log stream is empty, so confirmation must come from frontend logs and traces.
proposal.risk: If the real mechanism is a bad deploy or OOM, the recreate destroys the exited container's exit code and logs — the only remaining evidence of why cart died — and cart comes back only to die again, costing time with no diagnosis. If 172.18.0.19:7070 is not cart, this restarts a healthy service for nothing. The action is not reversible and discards cart's in-process cache, causing a brief cold-cache latency bump.
proposal.blast_radius: cart only, for the duration of the recreate. Its callers checkout and frontend see connection resets during the restart — they are already failing against it, so the marginal harm is small. Downstream of checkout (payment, shipping, currency, product-catalog, email) will begin receiving traffic again if the fix works, which is itself a change in their load.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service failure spanning the frontend path and checkout, with load-generator also affected, indicating user-visible impact. No open incident covers it and the alerts do not point to a single fault class yet.
